query: Starting from a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, what single intervention could overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength? The hypothesis should address the tendency for dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries to produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage during straining. Specify the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted strength and ductility relative to the untreated starting material, the applicable testing and operating conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

revised_generation.hypothesis: Introducing discrete B2 precipitates within a continuous BCC matrix in refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) can improve room temperature tensile ductility while maintaining high yield strength at both room and elevated temperatures.
revised_generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) with a two-phase ordered B2 + BCC microstructure and a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
revised_generation.intervention: Microstructural engineering to form an "inverted" BCC + B2 microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates dispersed within a continuous BCC matrix.
revised_generation.structural_mediator: Discrete B2 precipitates within a continuous BCC matrix.
revised_generation.mechanism: Improved room temperature tensile ductility due to the change in microstructure, which reduces the tendency for dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries and thereby decreases local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage during straining.
revised_generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room temperature tensile ductility and maintained high yield strength at both room and elevated temperatures.
revised_generation.baseline: Typical RHEAs with a two-phase ordered B2 + BCC microstructure.
revised_generation.boundary: Limited to refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
revised_generation.uncertainty: Further research is needed to confirm the effectiveness of this approach in different RHEAs and to understand the underlying mechanisms. Additionally, the impact of this microstructural engineering on other properties, such as fatigue resistance and corrosion resistance, needs to be investigated.
revised_generation.falsification_experiment: Comparing the mechanical properties of RHEAs with the inverted microstructure to those with the typical two-phase ordered B2 + BCC microstructure, with a focus on room temperature tensile ductility and yield strength.

cited_evidence.text:
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) can have either high strength or high ductility, and a simultaneous achievement of both still constitutes a tough challenge. The inferior castability and compositional segregation of HEAs are also obstacles for their technological applications. To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept, i.e. to achieve a microstructure composed of alternating soft fcc and hard bcc phases. As a manifestation of this concept, an AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 (atomic portion) eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was designed. The as-cast EHEA possessed a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure, and showed an unprecedented combination of high tensile ductility and high fracture strength at room temperature. The excellent mechanical properties could be kept up to 700°C. This new alloy design strategy can be readily adapted to large-scale industrial production of HEAs with simultaneous high fracture strength and high ductility.

Typically, refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), comprising a two-phase ordered B2 + BCC microstructure, exhibit extraordinarily high yield strengths, but poor ductility at room temperature, limiting their engineering application. The poor ductility is attributed to the continuous matrix being the ordered B2 phase in these alloys. This paper presents a novel approach to microstructural engineering of RHEAs to form an “inverted” BCC + B2 microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates dispersed within a continuous BCC matrix, resulting in improved room temperature compressive ductility, while maintaining high yield strength at both room and elevated temperature.
